title: My Lovely School · independent Lesson 3 test

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: School and house place vocabulary
questions.prompt: 1. Omar sleeps in this room at home. What is it called?
questions.evidence: A bedroom is the room for sleeping. A kitchen and a laboratory have different uses.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: School and house place vocabulary
questions.prompt: 2. Lina wants to borrow a book for the weekend. Which place should she visit?
questions.evidence: A library is the place for borrowing and reading books.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Sorting school and house places
questions.prompt: 3. Choose True or False: a playground belongs in the school box, not the house box.
questions.evidence: In this lesson, playground is grouped with school places; the house box contains rooms such as bedroom, kitchen and living room.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Asking and answering about location
questions.prompt: 4. Look at this new row of rooms. Which room is in the middle?
questions.evidence: The library is between the art room and the music room, so it is the middle room.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Asking and answering about location
questions.prompt: 5. This row is arranged from left to right. Which statement describes it?
options: a) The music room is on the left of the gym.
b) The gym is on the left of the music room.
c) The gym is between two libraries.
questions.evidence: The music room is the left-hand box and the gym is the right-hand box. There is only one gym and no pair of libraries.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Asking and answering about location
questions.prompt: 6. Use the floor list. Choose True or False: to visit the cafeteria, go downstairs.
questions.evidence: The floor list puts the cafeteria and gym downstairs, and the library and art room upstairs.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Using there is and there are
questions.prompt: 7. Complete: “There ___ a kitchen in this house.”
questions.evidence: A kitchen is singular, so the correct form is there is.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Using there is and there are
questions.prompt: 8. Choose the beginning of the sentence: “___ two libraries in the new building.”
questions.evidence: Two libraries is plural, so use there are.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Understanding lesson quantities
questions.prompt: 9. Read Omar’s classroom count. How many chairs are there?
questions.evidence: The chairs row shows 25. The 20 belongs to books, and 2 belongs to desks.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Expressing abilities and preferences
questions.prompt: 10. Noor wants to make a picture of her classroom on paper. Complete: “I can ___ a picture.”
questions.evidence: Draw is the action used for making a picture.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: School and house place vocabulary
questions.prompt: 11. Choose True or False: a kitchen is a place for sleeping.
questions.evidence: A kitchen is for preparing food; a bedroom is for sleeping. The statement is false.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Recognising and building the ea words
questions.prompt: 12. Which letter pair is highlighted in both m-eat and eat in this lesson?
questions.evidence: The lesson highlights ea in meat and eat. The other pairs are not the target pair.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading an unseen school description
questions.prompt: 13. Read Hana’s school description. Which room is upstairs?
questions.evidence: The description says that the library is upstairs. It does not put the art room upstairs, and the playground is outside.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading an unseen school description
questions.prompt: 14. Read Hana’s school description. Choose True or False: there are twenty desks in the library.
questions.evidence: The library has twenty books but only two desks, so the statement is false.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading an unseen school description
questions.prompt: 15. Read Hana’s school description. Which room does Hana like best?
questions.evidence: Hana likes the art room best because she can draw there.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Asking for and giving help
questions.prompt: 16. Lina says, “I cannot find my classroom.” Choose the most helpful reply.
options: c) Yes, of course. It is upstairs.
questions.evidence: This reply offers help and gives the location of the classroom. The other replies do not help Lina find it.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Using there is and there are
questions.prompt: 17. Correct the verb in this new sentence: “There is two desks here.” Write only the correct verb.
questions.evidence: Two desks is plural, so is must change to are: There are two desks here.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Writing a clear English sentence
questions.prompt: 18. Write a sentence beginning with I. Use all four words exactly once: can / read / there / I.
questions.evidence: Beginning with I, the correct order is I + can + read + there. The sentence expresses an ability in a place.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Asking and answering about location
questions.prompt: 19. Write the lesson word that is the opposite of upstairs.
questions.evidence: Downstairs names the lower floor and is the opposite of upstairs in the lesson.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Recognising and building the ea words
questions.prompt: 20. Build the food word from the lesson: m + ea + t. Write the whole word.
questions.evidence: Joining m, ea and t makes meat, one of the two printed ea words.
